title: Grilled Provolone Provoleta with Oregano, Chilli and Toasted Bread
summary: A cold slab of provolone is seared in a very hot cast-iron pan until a brown crust forms, finished under the grill until bubbling, then scattered with oregano and chilli flakes and served in the pan with olive-oil toasted baguette.
equipment: 20 cm cast-iron frying pan (or a grill with a hot side)

ingredients.item: provolone in one round slab, about 2 cm thick
baguette, cut into 1 cm slices on the diagonal

steps.title: Keep it cold
steps.text: Keep the provolone in the fridge until the moment it goes in the pan.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Brush the baguette slices with oil and toast them under the grill.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat the cast-iron pan until very hot and brush it with oil.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Cook the cheese undisturbed until browned underneath, then add half the herbs.

steps.title: Finish under the grill
steps.text: Grill the top until bubbling and the centre is soft.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add the rest of the oregano and chilli and serve at once with the bread.

tips: A thick slab of firm provolone works best; thin or soft cheese melts into a puddle.
Do not move the cheese while it sears, or the crust will tear.
Serve it in the pan on a board so it stays molten at the table.
storage: Provoleta is best eaten immediately. Leftovers can be chilled for up to 2 days and melted onto toast, though they will not ooze the same way again. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
